claims.text: The NE clamp enforces |γ_NE|·g_NE ≤ 0.5 for either sign of γ_NE, keeps 1 + γ_NE·g_NE in [0.5, 1.5], and so never drives a positive threshold to zero.

claims.text: The canonical drive Π_rel·(|z| − m₀) is monotone in Π_rel if and only if |z| ≥ m₀; below m₀ it is strictly decreasing, so more precision on a smaller-than-expected error makes ignition harder. Equal-magnitude errors of opposite sign contribute equally.
claims.status_basis: added by the verification registry after the SSOT draft; enters the SSOT at D10

claims.status_basis: added by the verification registry after the SSOT draft; enters the SSOT at D10

claims.text: Divisive normalization keeps a budget of 2, reduces to the core at equal gains, and lowers exteroceptive gain when interoceptive gain rises.

claims.text: Urgency is non-negative, non-decreasing and vanishes at u_max = 0; P(report) lies in [g, 1 − λ_lapse] and rises with P(hit); the geometric and continuous timescale forms hit their endpoints and are monotone; ψ is bounded and odd; Γ = R² ∈ [0, 1]; aggregation stays between the extreme level drives; the hierarchical target stays in [0.5, 1.5]·θ₀,ℓ.

claims.text: Lyapunov conjecture (SSOT §12.5): V = Σ_ℓ[(Π_ℓ − Π_ℓ*)² + (θ_ℓ − θ_ℓ*)²] satisfies V̇ ≤ −λV with λ ≥ min(1/τ_Π, 1/τ_θ)·(1 − loop gain). Not proved; needs the closed-loop linearization.
claims.status_basis: added by the verification registry after the SSOT draft; enters the SSOT at D10

claims.text: Estimator rules: ε is antisymmetric and vanishes at x̂ = x; z vanishes at μ_ref, is odd about it and monotone in ε; α_EMA ∈ (0, 1); the EMA mean stays between μ and ε; the variance stays non-negative and only shrinks for a sample at the mean (mean-centred, not E[ε²]); Π_rel = 1 at Π̄ and inherits the clamp scaled by 1/Π̄.

claims.text: The soft floor σ(−γ_sig·θ_eff) is ≤ ε iff γ_sig·θ_eff ≥ log(1/ε − 1), so a floor ≤ 0.01 needs γ_sig·θ_eff ≥ log 99; the step rule dt ≤ τ/10 implies the forward-Euler bound.
claims.status_basis: added by the verification registry after the SSOT draft; enters the SSOT at D10

claims.text: Between events the continuous threshold form (and its reduced measurable form) is solved by θ* + (θ(0) − θ*)e^{−t/τ} with θ* = θ₀ + τ·D; T_ant = 0 recovers the reactive cost; V ≥ 0, C is monotone in the previous ignition, and more information value never raises the next threshold.

claims.text: The precision-ODE rate is strictly decreasing in Π_ℓ and reduces to pure decay without drive or coupling; level salience is sign-symmetric under the symmetric Ψ and monotone in the gate; a synchronized Kuramoto level drifts at ω; the tanh reservoir state is bounded and its readout is non-negative.

claims.text: E_L(310 K) = k_B·310·ln 2 lies within 0.5% of 2.97 × 10⁻²¹ J, and the 300 K value is below 2.88 × 10⁻²¹ J; κ = E_event/(N_b·|ΔG_ATP|) ≥ 0; R_L ≥ 1 iff E_event ≥ N_erase·E_L. These are unit and arithmetic facts, not measurements of neural efficiency.

claims.text: Along every trajectory of the canonical 15-step pipeline, for every input sequence and every sequence of uniform draws, Σ ≥ 0 in both channels, θ ≥ θ_floor, r ≥ 0, B_prev ∈ {0, 1}, S ≥ −m₀·(Π_max/Π̄ᵉ + Π_max/Π̄ⁱ), every precision stays in [Π_min, Π_max] and |γ_NE|·g_NE ≤ 0.5 (any reference estimator; admissible parameters). claims.text: The ignition decision at t (B_t and B(t)) does not depend on the inputs at t; under the rejected 17-step order 'ignition after accumulation' it depends strictly on the current drive, and 'statistics before standardization' shrinks z by (1 − α). The canonical and rejected orders are therefore not equivalent.

claims.text: Recovery bound used by the full-pipeline study (task 62b): a behavioral report (EQ-OBS-1/2) is a parameter-free randomized function of the every-step event sequence B(t), so the Fisher information it carries about any pipeline parameter is at most that of B(t) (data-processing inequality for Fisher information). A parameter unidentified from B(t) is therefore unidentified from reports.
evidence: standard result, not formalized here: Zamir, R. (1998), A proof of the Fisher information inequality via a data processing argument, IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory 44(3), 1246-1250
